name: Root
description: Minimal composition-only root component split across two files: main.tsx (side-effect-only entry point that bootstraps the React 18 application via createRoot) and App.tsx (exports the App component composing the provider hierarchy: StrictMode → ConvexProvider → BrowserRouter → Layout → Routes). Delegates all domain logic, type ownership, data access, and page rendering to child subsystems. Root owns no domain types; it references them by import only. Enforces the structural constraint that ConvexProvider wraps the entire routed tree, VITE_CONVEX_URL is validated at startup, exactly two leaf routes exist (index '/' → HomePage, dynamic '/:toolSlug' → ToolPage), and dependency flow is strictly unidirectional (root imports from children, children never import from root).

types.name: AppProps
types.description: Props interface for the root App component. Currently empty, reserved for forward compatibility (e.g., injecting a test Convex client or overriding the router for testing).

types.name: RootDivId
types.description: The DOM element ID used as the React mount point. Always 'root'. Corresponds to the div#root in index.html generated by project_scaffold.

types.name: ReactElement
types.description: Opaque React element type returned by component render functions. Represents the JSX tree produced by App or bootstrap.

types.name: ErrorBoundaryFallbackProps

fields.name: error
fields.description: The Error object or unknown value thrown by a child component or route loader.

types.description: Props interface for the root-level error boundary fallback component rendered via React Router errorElement. Displays a user-friendly error screen when an unrecoverable rendering error occurs in any child route.

types.name: RouteLeafCount
types.description: Integer representing the number of leaf routes in the route tree. Structurally constrained to exactly 2 (index route and dynamic :toolSlug route).

functions.name: App
functions.description: Root React functional component exported from src/App.tsx. Composes the full provider and routing hierarchy: React.StrictMode → ConvexProvider(client) → BrowserRouter → Routes → Route(path='/', element=<Layout />) with two child routes: Route(index, element=<HomePage />) and Route(path=':toolSlug', element=<ToolPage />). The ConvexReactClient is obtained by calling app_shell's createConvexClient() at module scope. Layout receives sidebar items derived from data_layer's getTools() mapped through app_shell's projectToolDefToSidebarItem(). A root-level errorElement renders a user-friendly error fallback. This component is the single composition root; it contains zero domain logic.

inputs.name: props
inputs.description: Currently empty props object. Accepts no configuration; all wiring is internal via child subsystem imports.

error_cases.name: convex_client_unavailable
error_cases.condition: createConvexClient() threw because VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable is missing, empty, or malformed.

error_data.message: App cannot render: Convex client failed to initialize. Ensure VITE_CONVEX_URL is set in .env.local.

error_cases.name: tool_registry_empty
error_cases.condition: data_layer getTools() returns an empty array or fewer than 11 entries, preventing sidebar construction.

error_data.message: App cannot render: Tool registry returned fewer than 11 entries. Data layer may be misconfigured.

error_cases.name: child_import_failure
error_cases.condition: One or more child component modules (HomePage, ToolPage, Layout) fail to resolve at import time.

error_data.message: App cannot render: Failed to import one or more child components.

preconditions: ConvexReactClient singleton has been successfully created (VITE_CONVEX_URL was valid at module load time).
All child components (HomePage, ToolPage, Layout, Sidebar) are importable from their respective modules.
data_layer getTools() returns exactly 11 ToolDef entries.
app_shell projectToolDefToSidebarItem is importable and correctly maps ToolDef to SidebarItem.
postconditions: Returns a single React element tree rooted in React.StrictMode.
ConvexProvider wraps the entire BrowserRouter and its descendants.
Route tree contains exactly 2 leaf routes: index ('/' → HomePage) and dynamic ('/:toolSlug' → ToolPage).
Layout route is the parent of both leaf routes and receives Outlet for child rendering.
Sidebar items array has exactly 11 entries, one per tool, sorted by step ascending.
An errorElement is attached to the root route to catch unrecoverable render errors.
No domain logic (data fetching, validation, formatting) is performed within this component.

functions.name: bootstrap
functions.description: Side-effect-only entry point function in src/main.tsx. Performs the one-time application mount: calls ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!) and renders <App /> into it. This function is not exported; it executes as a top-level side effect when main.tsx is loaded by the Vite module bundler. Corresponds to the module script src='/src/main.tsx' referenced in index.html.

error_cases.condition: document.getElementById('root') returns null because index.html is misconfigured or div#root was removed.

error_data.message:

error_cases.name: react_dom_unavailable
error_cases.condition: react-dom/client module cannot be resolved, indicating missing or incompatible React 18 installation.

error_data.message: Failed to import react-dom/client. Ensure react-dom@18.x is installed.

error_cases.name: app_import_failure
error_cases.condition: App component module cannot be resolved from main.tsx.

error_data.message: Failed to import App component. Check that src/App.tsx exists and exports a default or named App component.

preconditions: document.getElementById('root') returns a non-null HTMLElement (index.html contains <div id='root'>).
React 18 createRoot API is available (react-dom/client is importable).
App component is importable from ./App or @/App.
postconditions: React 18 root is created and mounted to the div#root DOM element.
App component tree is rendered, triggering ConvexProvider connection and BrowserRouter initialization.
No return value; function is purely side-effectful.
Subsequent calls to createRoot on the same element would throw (single-mount invariant).
side_effects: Mounts React application into the DOM, creating a persistent React root.

structured_side_effects.description: Creates a React 18 root and renders the App component tree into the #root div, replacing any existing content.

functions.name: RootErrorFallback
functions.description: Error boundary fallback component rendered by React Router's errorElement on the root route. Displays a user-friendly error screen with a brief message and a link to navigate back to the home page. Accepts the thrown error via useRouteError() hook. Styled with Tailwind classes consistent with the dark terminal aesthetic.

inputs.name: props
inputs.description: Optional props. In practice, the error is obtained via useRouteError() rather than props, but the interface supports direct injection for testing.

error_cases.name: missing_router_context
error_cases.condition: Component rendered outside of a React Router context, causing useRouteError() to throw.

error_data.message: RootErrorFallback must be rendered within a React Router context.

preconditions: Component is rendered within a React Router v6 context that provides useRouteError().
postconditions: Renders a visible error message indicating something went wrong.
Provides a navigation link or button to return to the home page ('/').
Does not re-throw the error; acts as a terminal error boundary.
Styled consistently with the dark terminal aesthetic (dark background, light text).

invariants: Exactly one React 18 root is created per application lifecycle, in main.tsx bootstrap().
The App component is the sole composition root; all other components are reachable only as descendants of App.
ConvexProvider is always the outermost provider wrapping BrowserRouter — Convex hooks are available in every routed component.
The route tree contains exactly 2 leaf routes: index ('/' → HomePage) and ':toolSlug' ('/:toolSlug' → ToolPage), both children of the Layout route.
Root imports from child subsystems (app_shell, data_layer, home_page, tool_page); child subsystems never import from root (unidirectional dependency flow).
Root owns zero domain types — AppProps is the only type defined, and it is a structural placeholder.
All 11 sidebar items are derived from data_layer getTools() mapped through app_shell projectToolDefToSidebarItem(); no hardcoded tool metadata exists in root.
VITE_CONVEX_URL validation occurs at module load time via app_shell createConvexClient(); the app fails fast if the env var is missing.
The root-level errorElement ensures unrecoverable child rendering errors display a fallback UI rather than a white screen.
src/main.tsx is loaded as type='module' from index.html; bootstrap() executes as a top-level side effect, not as an exported callable.
Dev server runs on port 4000 as configured by project_scaffold in vite.config.ts.
All styling uses Tailwind CSS classes and inline style attributes for dynamic accent colors; no custom CSS files are created by root.

data_access.rationale: Root reads only PUBLIC-tier data: the static tool registry (11 ToolDef entries from data_layer getTools()) to construct sidebar navigation items, and the VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variable to initialize the Convex client. No PII, INTERNAL, or sensitive data is read or written by the root component. All Convex data access (comments with author names) is delegated to child components (tool_page CommentsSection) and governed by their own data_access declarations.

side_effects.rationale: Reads the Convex deployment URL from import.meta.env at module load time to initialize the ConvexReactClient singleton. This URL is a deployment configuration value, not sensitive data.
bootstrap() in main.tsx creates a React 18 root on the #root DOM element and renders the App component tree. This is a one-time side effect at application startup.
